title: Hierarchical API-key hysteresis and safe-reset reconciliation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Context: We’ve observed customer reports and internal telemetry indicating incorrect billable token counts during two classes of events: (1) transient spikes that cause hard throttles on API keys shared across many clients within an account, and (2) mid-window project/plan migrations where leftover reserved capacity is transferred between queues and double-counted during the next reset. Both lead to perceived overage invoices or unexpected 429s.

Goal: Implement a hierarchical quota model (account -> project -> api-key) with a concurrency-weighted replenishment algorithm and a hysteresis-based soft-escalation window to reduce harmful hard-throttles. Add a deterministic safe-reset protocol and a reconciliation job that consumes the ordered audit stream to correct any mis-applied credits or debits at window boundaries. The combined system should preserve billing correctness, reduce surprise throttles, and remain deterministic/idempotent under retries.

Proposed approach: 
1) Hierarchical model: introduce a light-weight quota tree keyed by (account_id, project_id, api_key). Each node stores: capacity, reserved_commit, used_in_window, last_checkpoint_nonce. The top-level account node enforces total reserved capacity; projects and keys inherit allocations.

2) Concurrency-weighted replenishment: instead of simple fixed-token replenishment on wall-clock ticks, replenish tokens proportional to the recent 1-minute average concurrency and per-request token cost. This reduces token starvation for high-concurrency, low-cost flows while preventing single long-running requests from monopolizing a burst bucket.

3) Hysteresis soft-escalation window: when an api-key exhausts its quota, instead of immediate hard-429, allow a short soft-window (configurable, default 10s) where requests are admitted up to a fractional extra budget computed from recent success rate and account-level headroom. Soft-admitted usage is tracked separately and billed but scored for later reconciliation. If the account headroom shrinks during the soft window, admission is cut off immediately.

4) Deterministic safe-reset protocol: at window boundary we run a two-phase checkpointed reset: (A) compute candidate deltas from per-key checkpoints in the ordered audit log (Kafka topic) up to watermark T, produce signed reset intents; (B) apply reset intents idempotently while writing out a reset-anchor record with monotonic nonce. This prevents double-credit when migration events reorder or replay. Reset intents include origin tags for reserved/dedicated pools to ensure proper prorate.

5) Reconciliation job: a background job consumes audit stream and compares applied deltas to expected (computed from request-level events). Discrepancies produce corrective ledger entries (debit/credit) and set a reconciliation-status on the key node. Corrections are surfaced to billing pipeline with reason codes (late-events, migration-prorate, soft-window-admit).

Data model changes: add fields to quota table: last_checkpoint_nonce (string), soft_window_consumed (integer), concurrency_weight (float), reconciliation_status (string). Add an append-only per-key ledger in object store for auditability (sharded by account).

APIs & operational controls: 
- GET /quota/{account}/usage returns hierarchical breakdown and soft-window allowances.
- Admin endpoints to force reanchor/reset: POST /admin/quotas/reset-anchor with nonce and dry_run.
- Flags to tune soft-window length, concurrency smoothing half-life, and max-soft-fraction per account.

Migration plan: 
- Phase A (read-only telemetry): deploy change to emit additional telemetry (concurrency metrics, soft-window admits, candidate reset intents) without changing enforcement. Monitor dashboards for signal and simulate reconciler against historical stream.
- Phase B (soft enforcement): enable soft-window admission for a subset (pilot) of accounts. Increase pilot size based on error/latency signals.
- Phase C (safe-reset rollout): enable deterministic safe-reset on low-risk clusters and run reconciliation job in dry-run then corrective mode.
- Phase D (global): flip enforcement to full hierarchical quota and safe-reset.

Monitoring & alerts: new dashboards: per-account soft-window admits, soft-fraction ratio, reconciliation drift, reset-anchor lag, late-event correction volume. Alerts: >0.5% of requests admitted by soft-window for >10 accounts in 5m, reconciliation corrections/sec > threshold, reset-anchor kafka lag > 30s.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Deterministic resets produce idempotent anchor records and no double-credit in 1000 synthetic migration test runs.
- Soft-window reduces visible hard-429s by at least 40% in pilot accounts without increasing corrected billing discrepancy above 0.5%.
- Reconciler corrects >95% of deliberately injected late-events within 1 hour and surfaces human-readable reason codes.
- All new fields are backward-compatible and migrations include zero-downtime scripts.

Risks & mitigations: 
- Risk: Soft-window could mask abusive traffic. Mitigation: rate-limit soft admits per account and flag abnormal admit patterns for review.
- Risk: Reconciler may overwhelm billing pipeline with corrections. Mitigation: throttle corrective ledger writes and batch with priority.
- Risk: Complexity in reset protocol. Mitigation: keep reset anchor compact and add extensive unit/integration tests and chaos tests on the ordered audit stream.

Rollout rollback plan: revert to Phase A instrumentation-only mode; expire soft-window admits by config; reapply previous simple reset logic if persistent irreconcilable errors are observed.
